inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,515 normalized logical lines in order. The article is mathematically coherent despite formula-glyph loss in a few displayed expressions: prose, theorem numbering, and neighboring formulas recover the two scale regimes, the random-matrix/prime-sum parallel, the zero-counting consequences, and the branching covariance construction. Front matter, page furniture, routine estimates, and references are explicitly accounted for; formula-dependent units record their extraction risk.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata and an abstract-level statement of the multidimensional zeta CLT, mesoscopic zero fluctuations, and unitary-matrix analogy.

sections_inspected.label: 1.1 Main result
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the multivariate mesoscopic CLT, its scale-indexed covariance, examples, Gaussian-process limit, and Brownian-plus-disorder realization.

sections_inspected.label: 1.2 Counting the zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers log-zeta fluctuations to centered zero counts and identifies the endpoint-increment covariance law.

sections_inspected.label: 1.3 Analogous result on random matrices
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the local-scale characteristic-polynomial analogue and its eigenvalue-counting consequence under n corresponding to log t.

sections_inspected.label: 1.4 Definitions and organization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fixes complex Gaussian, log-zeta, and log-characteristic-polynomial representations and announces the parallel proof architecture.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1-2.2 Matrix CLT and the regime epsilon_n much larger than 1/n
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the Diaconis-Evans trace CLT, Cramer-Wold reduction, and a logarithmic oscillatory sum to extract the covariance kernel.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3 Matrix CLT at or inside the 1/n scale
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Removes the radial regularization and proves the boundary-scale covariance by truncated harmonic exponential sums.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1 Selberg method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the short-Dirichlet-series approximation and reduces the zeta theorem to a Gaussian limit for weighted prime phases without assuming RH.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Number-theoretic Diaconis-Evans analogue
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Establishes an L2-tail criterion and a growing-dimensional time-to-torus moment comparison for prime sums.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3 Zeta proof when epsilon_t is much larger than 1/log t
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Verifies the prime-sum CLT hypotheses and derives the off-axis covariance from the pole of zeta.

sections_inspected.label: 3.4 Zeta proof at or inside the 1/log t scale
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Removes the small abscissa shift and evaluates the critical-scale prime covariance through the prime number theorem.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Spatial branching connection
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Realizes the minimum-along-an-interval covariance as Brownian diffusion on a tree and gives an explicit discrete Gaussian recursion.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography only; no new source-level semantic mechanism.

accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. Read with lines 138-172 for concrete two-point scale interpretation; the theorem statement itself is present here.

accepted_units.title: Log-zeta fluctuations as mesoscopic zero-count fluctuations
accepted_units.why_material: It converts imaginary log-zeta increments into centered counts and shows that shrinking interval scales retain Gaussian fluctuations distinct from microscopic repulsion.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span terminates as the covariance is introduced; lines 261-291 are required to complete and interpret the result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the explicit counting formula (1.8) and displayed process normalization; endpoint formulas have text-layer glyph loss but are identifiable from the checked prose.

accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 3.1 replaces full moment control by small coefficients, total L2 mass, and a negligible prime tail, providing the arithmetic analogue of a trace CLT.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span states the criterion and tail reduction but not the finite-prime equidistribution argument; lines 934-1168 supply the full mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on condition (3.2), the Montgomery-Vaughan mean-square estimate, and the displayed finite-prime limit; the surrounding prose makes the logical dependencies recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Off-axis prime covariance from the zeta pole
accepted_units.why_material: The proof selects a subpolynomial cutoff and turns the weighted prime covariance into log zeta near its pole, yielding the minimum-of-scales kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. Lines 1171-1273 restore the subsection heading and proof closure; Proposition 3.1 remains the upstream CLT input.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Lemma 3.3, prime-number-theorem tail control, the Euler product logarithm, and zeta(1+x) asymptotics; several display symbols require formula-aware reading.

accepted_units.title: Scale-indexed covariance as Brownian motion plus total disorder
accepted_units.why_material: The two-point examples expose how correlation varies with logarithmic separation, while the decomposition X_delta=B_delta+D_{1-delta} separates shared hierarchical fluctuation from independent disorder and proves nonmeasurability.
accepted_units.context_note: This interprets the covariance immediately after Theorem 1.1 and overlaps the opening of the carried zero-counting span only where the paper changes viewpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed two-point normal mixture and covariance kernel have minor glyph loss; the Brownian/disorder construction and Fubini contradiction are clear in prose. Scan verification is advisable for the piecewise kernel typography.

accepted_units.title: Endpoint increments produce the exotic zero-count covariance
accepted_units.why_material: Corollary 1.3 and its discussion show that interval-count correlations are governed by shared endpoints rather than interval inclusion, and construct the limit as D_beta-D_alpha from independent Gaussian coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the covariance statement cut off by carried unit u02 and includes the paper's interpretation of strict versus non-strict interval inclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on piecewise formula (1.9), whose cases are visually degraded; the endpoint-difference construction and prose recover the sign and independence mechanism, but exact case typography should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Local-scale characteristic-polynomial CLT and eigenvalue counts
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem matches radial and angular matrix shifts to zeta abscissa and ordinate shifts, extending n corresponding to log t to local covariance and interval-count statistics.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem, the n/log t dictionary, and the centered eigenvalue-count consequence; later sections provide the proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on formulas (1.10)-(1.11) and the log-characteristic-polynomial endpoint identity; slash and inequality glyphs are imperfect but the correspondence is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic representations that expose parallel matrix and zeta proofs
accepted_units.why_material: The branch choices and trace expansion make log Z a linear statistic, while the roadmap explicitly pairs the matrix trace CLT with the prime-sum proposition as strict analogues.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the local definitions needed to read subsequent trace and prime expansions without importing branch conventions from elsewhere.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the integral definition of log zeta and the trace power series/L2 boundary definition of log Z; the formulas are sufficiently legible despite summation glyph noise.

accepted_units.title: Diaconis-Evans converts trace decompositions into Gaussian limits
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem isolates variance convergence and negligible high-frequency mass as sufficient conditions, turning class-function CLTs into coefficient estimates after trace-basis decomposition.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the matrix-side reusable probabilistic engine for both radial regimes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the weighted coefficient conditions (2.1)-(2.2), including j wedge n; formula extraction is readable with the theorem prose.

accepted_units.title: Off-circle matrix covariance from a damped logarithmic kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Cramer-Wold reduces the vector theorem to one trace series, and Lemma 2.2 shows how damping and angular separation compete so a normalized logarithmic sum converges to c wedge 1.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the coefficient choice, variance split, kernel lemma, its scale cases, and the high-frequency cutoff verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense span relying on trace coefficients, a Taylor expansion of -log(1-X), and scale comparisons; prose supports the mechanism but exact exponents should be formula-checked.

accepted_units.title: On-circle matrix covariance from oscillatory harmonic sums
accepted_units.why_material: The proof shows radial regularization is boundedly negligible at the 1/n scale and evaluates the remaining truncated harmonic exponential sum across c>1, 0<c<1, c=1, and c=0.
accepted_units.context_note: The c=0 summation-by-parts bound is essential: it handles angular sequences that need not converge to zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Lemma 2.3 and several oscillatory integral comparisons; OCR drops some delta symbols, but the case analysis and estimates remain reconstructible from the span.

accepted_units.title: Selberg's L2 approximation reduces log zeta to a short prime sum
accepted_units.why_material: The section distinguishes the heuristic Euler-product independence from the rigorous step: an absolutely convergent explicit-formula modification gives an L2-short Dirichlet approximation without RH, after which Slutsky and Cramer-Wold isolate the prime-sum CLT.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the explicit RH caveat, Selberg's mean-square approximation, and the exact equivalent formulation of Theorem 1.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy explicit-formula displays are degraded, but the L2 bound, short prime sum, normalization, and logical use of Slutsky are clear in the checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Growing prime phases: from time averages to torus averages
accepted_units.why_material: The proof combines a triangular-array CLT for independent phases with quantitative Fourier control of time-versus-space averages, using unique factorization to bound near-resonances as the number of primes grows.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes carried Proposition 3.1 after its L2-tail reduction and records why log m_t=o(log t) is sufficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on moment polynomials, a torus Fourier expansion, and Lemma 3.2's lower bound for integer combinations of log primes; superscript glyphs are noisy but the unique-factorization argument is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line prime covariance from the prime number theorem
accepted_units.why_material: At epsilon_t at most order 1/log t the abscissa shift is negligible, and Lemma 3.4 turns the prime covariance into an oscillatory integral whose cutoff relative to log t again yields c wedge 1.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the number-theoretic counterpart of the boundary matrix Lemma 2.3 and completes the second regime of Theorem 1.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on partial summation with pi(x), the prime number theorem, and oscillatory-integral bounds; several delta symbols are missing, so exact displayed expressions merit formula-aware verification.

accepted_units.title: Minimum-along-path covariance realized by a Gaussian tree
accepted_units.why_material: The section explains positive semidefiniteness structurally: minimum covariance is common ancestral Brownian history, and the discrete father map yields an explicit independent-increment recursion with the prescribed covariance.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the continuous Le Gall tree analogy and the finite Gaussian construction needed for the paper's covariance matrix.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on formulas (4.1)-(4.3) and the ancestor/father definitions; one formula-number cross-reference appears inconsistent in extraction, but the construction and covariance claim are clear.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One logarithmic covariance kernel on the matrix and zeta sides
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Under the source's n-to-log-t correspondence, damped or truncated logarithmic sums on both sides convert relative evaluation-point scale into the same c wedge 1 covariance, with separate proofs above and below the natural boundary scale.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper proves matching limits for these observables; it does not establish a universal random-matrix model for all zeta statistics.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Counting statistics are endpoint differences of log observables
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both zero counts and unitary eigenvalue counts inherit Gaussian laws because a centered interval count is represented by the difference of imaginary logarithms at its endpoints, making shared endpoints control covariance.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The stated mesoscopic laws are distinct from microscopic pair-repulsion results and do not replace them.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parallel CLT engines after representation change
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Expanding log Z in traces and approximating log zeta by prime phases reduce both vector theorems to triangular-array Gaussian limits controlled by L2 mass and tail concentration, while arithmetic additionally requires quantitative time-to-torus comparison.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The arithmetic proposition has a different cutoff condition and uses unique factorization; the analogy is structural, not identity of proofs.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Covariance positivity through shared ancestry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The minimum-type covariance is made concrete by decomposing fluctuation into shared history plus independent increments, expressed once as Brownian/disordered components and once as diffusion or recursion on an ancestral tree.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The constructions realize the Gaussian covariance law; they do not derive the zeta theorem independently of the analytic arguments.
